inline:The target's iff criterion for distinguishing genuine reliability gain from mere compliance is satisfied by an unreliable (compliant-only) panel, so the criterion is unsound.
The target defines mere checklist compliance as outperformance due to the act of following a structured procedure regardless of rule content. Its corrupted-checklist control tests only whether rule content affects accuracy, not whether the panel engages in genuine scrutiny of those rules. A panel that passively conforms to whichever checklist it is given can still exhibit an accuracy gap between correct and corrupted rules, because correct rules simply point more often to the verifiable outcome. That gap is not evidence of genuine reliability; it is evidence of sensitivity to cue quality, which is fully compatible with compliance. The target's 'if and only if' therefore licenses the very compliance case it is supposed to distinguish. Within a single evaluation, the proposed control cannot tell whether the panel is applying judgment or merely executing the supplied rules, so it fails to distinguish genuine gain from mere compliance as required.
